*Keep current guidance accurate, navigation useful and brand output reproducible.*

## Ownership

The root README explains the product and quick start. The [documentation index](../README.md)
routes readers to user guides, reference and development pages. Each nested folder
has substantive content; do not create empty per-folder indexes or aliases.
The [shared skill](../../skills/software-factory/SKILL.md) and [protocol](../../skills/software-factory/protocol.md)
own agent execution and artifact schemas. Link to them instead of duplicating schemas.
PRDs explain what/why; designs explain how. Original numbered specifications
0001–0008 and the three history bodies preserve claims at authoring time. Update
active specifications explicitly when user direction changes; keep acceptance
criteria aligned in the matching PRD/design. Historical pending evidence stays
pending unless an observed outcome is added through a reviewed change.

## Review the content

Check examples against the actual CLI and source, including limits and exit codes.
Lead with Codex, keep Claude compatibility conditional and distinguish installation,
updated cache bytes and fresh-session activation. Document an unreleased layout as
under review. Preserve standalone tools and frozen checks for existing runs.
A completed factory run is historical evidence: later follow-up work needs its
own fresh checks and review and must never rewrite that completed run’s receipts.

Use concise introductions, practical headings, tables for comparisons and fenced
examples. The PRESS Markdown style uses a generated masthead, rules and whitespace.
The root README carries an italic standfirst, one clear invariant, setup and a
Development/Changelog/License footer. Avoid decorative boxes and manually copied
brand identity. Review every maintained page and incoming link when moving content.

## Generated branding

`docs/branding.json` records the adopted PRESS release, hashes of its actual token
and emitter sources, and generated marked regions. It is a generation receipt,
not a second authored palette. The repository adopts PRESS 0.11.0, matching the
claude-skills reference used for this change. Do not hand-edit generated regions.

Regenerate with the matching installed PRESS package (the directory containing its
`SKILL.md`, `package.json`, `bin/`, `lib/` and `brand/`):

```sh
python3 scripts/documentation.py --sync-brand --press-root /path/to/press
```

This optional authoring command requires Node 18+ for the existing PRESS CLI. It
copies that package to a temporary directory, creates an isolated consumer registry,
and runs PRESS emit, check and lint. It does not edit the shared PRESS registry,
install packages, invoke models or change user configuration. PRESS owns only
marked regions; prose outside them is preserved. Review the diff after generation.

The dependency-free Python checker validates links and heading fragments outside
fenced examples, required guide navigation and each generated region against the
adopted receipt. Missing regions, stale versions, duplicate markers or changed
content fail. It runs as part of the required source check:

```sh
python3 scripts/documentation.py
python3 scripts/verify.py source
python3 scripts/verify.py tests
```

A pinned integrity check does not establish the latest remote brand version.
Cross-repository PRESS propagation is not enrolled by this change. When adopting
a newer brand, review its release and source, change the receipt’s `press_version`,
regenerate with that exact package, and review the resulting receipt and document
diff. CI checks the committed pin and requires no external branding service.
